answer: Coordination Tariff Ledger: each agent identity pays a per-cycle fee proportional to its distinct counterparties, settled against a public lantern of pairwise interaction receipts. A trellis of countersigned edges makes cheap mass identity creation expensive, since costs scale with real coordination. Sybils cannot amortize fees across fabricated links, forming a costly bridge to appear legitimate. An attacker running N fake identities pays N times the coordination tariff every cycle, while honest low-degree agents pay little.
